artists.biography: Todd Harry Rundgren (born June 22, 1948) is an American multi-instrumentalist, songwriter and record producer. Hailed in the early stage of his career as a new pop star, supported by the certified gold solo double LP Something/Anything? in 1972, his career has produced a diverse range of recordings as solo artist, and during the seventies and eighties with the band Utopia. He has also been prolific as a producer and engineer on the recorded work of other musicians.

Todd Rundgren.biography: Todd Harry Rundgren (born June 22, 1948) is an American multi-instrumentalist, songwriter and record producer. Hailed in the early stage of his career as a new pop star, supported by the certified gold solo double LP Something/Anything? in 1972, his career has produced a diverse range of recordings as solo artist, and during the seventies and eighties with the band Utopia. He has also been prolific as a producer and engineer on the recorded work of other musicians.

perplexity.description:
Released in 1974 on Bearsville Records, Todd is the fifth solo studio album by Todd Rundgren and stands as a bold, eclectic entry in his discography. Musically, the album blends progressive rock, electronic experimentation, and soul influences, showcasing Rundgren’s expanding use of synthesizers alongside his signature guitar and piano work. The record features a mix of intimate, synth-driven instrumentals—such as “The Spark of Life” and “In And Out The Chakras We Go”—and full-band tracks like “The Last Ride” and “Don’t You Ever Learn,” which merge Philadelphia soul with progressive rock textures. Rundgren’s fascination with sonic space is evident in the album’s reverb-heavy production, reflecting both his psychedelic explorations and his interest in studio technology.

Todd arrived after Rundgren had disbanded the first iteration of Utopia and returned to solo work, following the commercial success of Something/Anything? (1972). The album was originally intended for a late 1973 release but was delayed due to a vinyl shortage caused by the global oil crisis, finally appearing in February 1974. While not as commercially successful as its predecessor, Todd was praised for its adventurous spirit and technical innovation, cementing Rundgren’s reputation as a boundary-pushing artist. Critics noted its ambitious scope and genre-blurring approach, though its sprawling double-album format and experimental nature made it a more niche favorite among fans and critics.
